newsitem.title: USA: Weak dlr said aided US competitiveness since 1985.
newsitem.headline: Weak dlr said aided US competitiveness since 1985.

text.p: The fall of the dollar over the past decade has helped make the U.S. economy more competitive, but it is not the only factor involved, the Competitiveness Council said on Tuesday.

The council, which groups business, labor and academic leaders, said that corporate restructuring and a reduced federal budget deficit were other factors that have played a role in America's increased competitiveness.
While the dollar has fallen against the mark and the yen since 1985, it has risen against the currencies of regional trading partners Mexico and Canada, the council added.
"There are a lot of other factors involved," council President John Yochelson told reporters, noting that growth in U.S. unit labor costs has been "extremely slow" since 1985.
W.R. Timken, Chairman of Timken Co, warned of the dangers of the United States relying on a weak dollar to enhance its competitiveness.
"If you come to rely on a dollar that may -- I think it's debatable -- be undervalued, you get a false sense of competitive security," the head of the bearing and special steel producer said.
"I'm not one of those who believe the dollar is terribly undervalued, in fact, I'd like to see it stay where it is," Timken added. "We'll see, but we can't rely on it."
The dollar has risen over the past 1-1/2 years against the mark and the yen, but it is still well below levels seen in 1985.
